persona: First-day Assessment Reviewer who is also the system Admin (roles REVIEWER + ADMIN), 13-inch laptop (~1280 CSS px wide). Knows the Caltrans GeoTech review job and the admin duties (accounts, road-inventory releases) but has never opened ERIS and had no training. Signs in and lands on /my-work (web/src/pages/LoginPage.tsx:42); header shows the raw string 'REVIEWER · ADMIN' as their identity (web/src/ui/AppShell.tsx:157). Because ADMIN satisfies every gate (web/src/utils/roleModel.ts:32-73), My Work loads the office-chief, branch-chief, engineer, reviewer, APPROVED and all-SUBMITTED queues plus every triage incident into one list (web/src/features/myWork/MyWorkPage.tsx:52-61).

tasks.task: Find the assessments submitted for my review, read the technical submission with its photos and map, and approve or return it
steps: Sign in; land on My Work. Read 'N items waiting on your role' and a rail that starts with red 'New report' triage cards (triage sorts first, MyWorkPage.tsx:71) — the auto-selected detail panel is a triage item titled 'Field report #N — not yet in the incident record' with a 'Start triage' button, not a review.

Scroll the rail looking for something that says 'review'. Recognise the brand-blue mini badge 'Submitted for review' and the line 'Waiting on Reviewer' (AssessmentDetailPanel.tsx:434-437) among 'Pending office delegation', 'Pending engineer assignment', 'Draft', 'Approved' cards. No filter or search exists (MyWorkPage.tsx:139-170).

Click the card. Detail panel shows 'Assessment #N', pipeline, a 'Next step — Waiting on Reviewer' box with the sentence 'Review the technical submission — approve it or request revision.', an 'Optional workflow notes' textarea and two buttons: 'Request revision' (red text) and 'Approve assessment' (green) (AssessmentDetailPanel.tsx:261-265, 294, 323-324).

Realise the form itself is not here; scroll to the 'Technical submissions (1)' card (hint 'All GISA forms attached to this assessment's incident') and click the blue 'Review' button in the Action column (AssessmentDetailPanel.tsx:336-357).

Arrive at /submissions/:id. Page title is the descriptor (e.g. 'D07-Los Angeles-R001-PM 12.30 - 2026-08-17', SubmissionDetailPage.tsx:1169). Header: '← Assessment #N', raw badge 'SUBMITTED' + 'Ready for reviewer decision', a '3 photos · 2 mapped' button, 'Refresh', 'Return for correction', 'Approve submission' (SubmissionDetailHeader.tsx:85-140).

Scroll: 'Location and ERIS map' hero with the ArcGIS map, submission point and mapped photos with heading wedges (SubmissionLocationHero.tsx:66-106); then the 'GISA Sheet' drag/resize card canvas whose inputs are all greyed because the fieldset is disabled for non-editors (SubmissionDetailPage.tsx:108, 725, 765-769); then 'Notes and actions'; then 'Submission library' with All/Photos/Videos/Documents tabs (SubmissionLibrary.tsx:8-13); optionally click '3 photos · 2 mapped' to open /submissions/:id/photo-evidence.
Keep scrolling to the bottom card grid: 'Summary', 'Reviewer Note' ('Recorded with the approval or return decision.') and 'Workflow History' (SubmissionReviewerSupport.tsx:24-38). Type the note here.

Scroll back to the top header and click 'Approve submission' (or 'Return for correction'). No confirmation; page reloads; badge becomes 'APPROVED' or 'REJECTED' (SubmissionDetailPage.tsx:375; SubmissionDetailPrimitives.tsx:3-17).

Notice the assessment in My Work still shows 'Submitted for review · Waiting on Reviewer'. Click '← Assessment #N' (goes to the read-only /assessments/:id record view, SubmissionDetailHeader.tsx:78-79), click 'This step is yours — act on it in My Work' (AssessmentDetailPanel.tsx:269), then click 'Approve assessment' or 'Request revision' on the assessment panel (AssessmentDetailPanel.tsx:323-324).

frictionPoints.problem: The admin flag turns My Work into a firehose: triage reports, office-chief delegations, branch-chief assignments, engineer drafts, APPROVED finalizations and every SUBMITTED assessment are merged into one unfiltered list, and the first item auto-selected is a coordinator triage panel.
frictionPoints.whyConfusing: A reviewer expects 'my review inbox'. Instead the header says 'items waiting on your role' and shows steps that belong to other jobs (MyWorkPage.tsx:52-61, 71, 88). There is no way to filter to 'Submitted for review' (MyWorkPage.tsx:139-170), so the newcomer must learn the badge colours to find their work.

frictionPoints.problem: Card says 'Waiting on Reviewer' for every SUBMITTED assessment, never 'Waiting on you', and does not say whether this user holds a REVIEWER/APPROVER assignment.
frictionPoints.whyConfusing: waitingOn() returns the generic role word (assessmentModel.ts:85-86) and the admin flag grants review permission regardless of assignment (assessmentModel.ts:131), so the user cannot tell which submissions were actually assigned to them versus everything in the state. The Assignments card further down is the only clue (AssessmentDetailPanel.tsx:366-388).

frictionPoints.problem: 'Approve assessment' and 'Request revision' are presented before the user has seen any of the technical content; the form lives on a different page reached from a table row.
frictionPoints.whyConfusing: The Next-step box (AssessmentDetailPanel.tsx:261-265, 321-326) reads like the whole task, and both buttons fire with a single click and no confirmation (323-324). A newcomer can approve blind. The 'Review' link to the actual form is one card lower, styled like a table action (357).

frictionPoints.problem: Vocabulary switches from 'Assessment' to 'Submission' / 'GISA Sheet' / 'GISA form' / 'technical submission', and the page title is a location-date descriptor rather than 'Submission #N'.
frictionPoints.whyConfusing: The nav highlights 'Assessments' while the URL says /submissions (AppShell.tsx:87), the header hint says 'GISA forms' (AssessmentDetailPanel.tsx:336), and the page heading is 'D07-Los Angeles-R001-PM 12.30 - <date>' (SubmissionDetailPage.tsx:1169). Nothing tells a first-day user that these three nouns are the same object.

frictionPoints.problem: The read-only form renders as a disabled edit form inside a drag/resize card canvas with toolbar hints 'Drag a card by its header · resize from the edges', 'Tidy layout', 'Reset layout', 'Full screen'.
frictionPoints.whyConfusing: Greyed inputs (fieldset disabled, SubmissionDetailPage.tsx:108, 725) look like a loading or permission problem rather than 'review mode'; the layout tools (762-794) are engineer-authoring affordances that a reviewer does not need and that suggest they should be editing.

frictionPoints.problem: Photos appear in three places with different labels: the header stat-button '3 photos · 2 mapped', the map hero, and the 'Submission library' near the bottom; the photo-evidence page is a separate route.
frictionPoints.whyConfusing: A button whose label is a statistic (SubmissionDetailHeader.tsx:71-75, 119-121) does not read as 'open the photo map'; 'unmapped' red pill (100-104) is unexplained jargon; the library is below the entire form (SubmissionDetailPage.tsx:1288).

frictionPoints.problem: The 'Reviewer Note' textarea is in the last card grid at the bottom of a very long page, while the Approve / Return buttons that consume it are in the top header.
frictionPoints.whyConfusing: The coupling is only stated in a subtitle ('Recorded with the approval or return decision.', SubmissionReviewerSupport.tsx:24) and review() reads reviewNote from that box (SubmissionDetailPage.tsx:375). A newcomer clicking 'Return for correction' from the header returns the form with an empty note, so the engineer gets no reason.

frictionPoints.problem: There are two different approvals: 'Approve submission' / 'Return for correction' on the submission header (POST /submissions/{id}/review → APPROVED / REJECTED) and 'Approve assessment' / 'Request revision' on the assessment panel (POST /assessments/{id}/review → APPROVED / REVISION_REQUESTED). Nothing says which is the workflow decision or whether one implies the other.
frictionPoints.whyConfusing: Labels, objects and resulting statuses all differ (SubmissionDetailHeader.tsx:135-140 and SubmissionDetailPage.tsx:375 vs AssessmentDetailPanel.tsx:323-324; badge text 'REJECTED' at SubmissionDetailPrimitives.tsx:15 vs 'Revision requested' at assessmentModel.ts:58). After approving the submission the My Work card still says 'Waiting on Reviewer', so the user believes the action failed or repeats it on the other object. This is the point where the walkthrough stalls.

frictionPoints.step: Getting back to the assessment action
frictionPoints.problem: The back link '← Assessment #N' lands on the read-only record view, which then sends the user to My Work via 'This step is yours — act on it in My Work'.
frictionPoints.whyConfusing: Two hops to return to the panel they came from (SubmissionDetailHeader.tsx:78-79; AssessmentDetailPanel.tsx:267-270); the browser back button would have been faster but nothing says so.

frictionPoints.problem: 'Request revision' silently submits the note 'Revision requested.' when the workflow-notes box is empty.
frictionPoints.whyConfusing: The textarea is labelled 'Optional workflow notes' (AssessmentDetailPanel.tsx:294), so a reviewer reasonably skips it, and the engineer receives a revision with no content (323).

frictionPoints.problem: Submission status is rendered as the raw enum ('SUBMITTED', 'REJECTED') while assessment state is humanised ('Submitted for review', 'Revision requested').
frictionPoints.whyConfusing: SubmissionStatusBadge prints the code verbatim (SubmissionDetailPrimitives.tsx:14-15); the same row in the assessment panel mixes both styles (AssessmentDetailPanel.tsx:353).

tasks.task: Create a new user account and give it the branch-chief role
steps: In the sidebar find 'Administration › Users' and click it (AppShell.tsx:93-99). Page title reads 'User Administration' (AdminUsersOperationsPage.tsx:173).

Scan four count cards (Accounts / Active / Inactive / Administrators) and the banner 'ERIS access management — Create accounts, manage operational roles, reset passwords, and disable access.' with a blue 'New account' button (175-188).
Click 'New account'. An inline section 'Create ERIS account' expands with Email *, Full name *, Initial password * and an 'Initial roles' chip row (190-200).
Type email, full name and invent an initial password (no rules shown, no generate button, no invite-by-email option).

In 'Initial roles', click the chip labelled 'Branch Chief' (legacy code BRANCH_CHIEF) or 'Geotech Branch Chief' (canonical GEOTECH_BRANCH_CHIEF) — whichever the /admin/roles list contains; hover shows the raw code as a tooltip (238-251).

Click 'Create account'. Green notice 'Created account for <name>.' appears, the form closes and the new row shows in the table with its role chips and 'Save roles' / 'Reset password' / 'Disable' actions (111-113, 220-225).
Tell the new user their email and initial password out of band.

frictionPoints.problem: Nav says 'Users' but the page is titled 'User Administration'; the header identity shows raw role codes, so the admin has no model of what a 'humanised' role looks like before reaching this page.
frictionPoints.whyConfusing: Minor label drift (AppShell.tsx:97 vs AdminUsersOperationsPage.tsx:173); the shell prints 'REVIEWER · ADMIN' (AppShell.tsx:157) while this page prints 'Reviewer' / 'Admin' via a local roleLabel (8-10).

frictionPoints.problem: Role chips are the humanised enum names from /admin/roles; legacy and canonical names can both appear ('Branch Chief' and 'Geotech Branch Chief'), and legacy 'Field Worker' actually means the GeoTech engineer while 'Maintenance' means the field reporter.
frictionPoints.whyConfusing: roleLabel only title-cases the code (AdminUsersOperationsPage.tsx:8-10); there is no description per chip and no indication that canonical and legacy names are aliases (backend/app/roles.py:1-27, 49-56). A newcomer picks one, or both, and cannot verify which the workflow gating expects.

frictionPoints.problem: Roles are pill-shaped checkbox labels with the checkbox visually hidden; nothing says 'select one or more'.
frictionPoints.whyConfusing: Pills read as tags, not toggles (238-251); the only validation is a page banner 'Select at least one role for the new account.' after clicking Create (101-104).

frictionPoints.problem: Admin must invent and later transmit an initial password; no password policy, strength hint, generator, show/hide toggle or invitation email.
frictionPoints.whyConfusing: The field is just 'Initial password *' (196). A server-side policy rejection would surface only as a raw error banner (114-115), and the login page tells users 'contact your application administrator' (LoginPage) so the admin is now the password courier.

frictionPoints.problem: Validation and API errors render in the page-level banner below the create section and the search row, not next to the field.
frictionPoints.whyConfusing: Errors at AdminUsersOperationsPage.tsx:209 are after the form (190-201); on a 13-inch screen with the form expanded they may sit just off the bottom.

frictionPoints.problem: The success notice names the person but does not scroll to or highlight the new row, and the table order is whatever the API returned.
frictionPoints.whyConfusing: Notice text at 111; the admin must use the search box (204) to confirm the roles stuck.

steps: Click 'Administration › Road Inventory' (AppShell.tsx:98). Page title 'Road Inventory'; hero card 'Authoritative roadway reference — Road inventory operations' with a 'Refresh state' button (RoadInventoryWorkspacePage.tsx:121-134).
Read four summary cards: 'Authoritative version', 'Mobile package Ready/Not ready', 'Pending versions — Imported, not authoritative', 'Superseded — Available for rollback' (136-141).
Skip past 'Current authoritative dataset' (Version / Segments / Extract date / Published plus a 'Mobile package' box with 'Generate mobile package' or 'Regenerate package') (146-179).

Reach 'Import road inventory — Upload an authoritative Excel extract. Successful imports remain pending until an administrator explicitly publishes a version.' Choose the .xlsx file, optionally type a 'Version tag' (placeholder 'Optional, e.g. 2026-08-17'), click 'Start import' (RoadInventoryImportPanel.tsx:111-145).
Watch the job card: badge 'queued' → 'processing' with a monospace stage code on the right, then 'succeeded' with '12,345 rows imported; 3 skipped. Dataset #14 is pending publication.' (150-156).
Scroll down to 'Dataset versions — Only one version is authoritative at a time…' and find the row whose Status is 'pending'; click its outlined 'Publish' button (183-199).

Confirmation dialog 'Authoritative dataset change — Publish road inventory version' lists Target version / Dataset ID / Rows / Current status, explains 'This will make X the authoritative road inventory… The currently published version Y will no longer be authoritative.' and 'After this change, regenerate the mobile road-inventory package if field devices need the new authoritative dataset.' Click 'Publish version' (RoadInventoryVersionActionDialog.tsx:26-72).

Green notice 'Published road inventory version X.' (104). Scroll back up: the 'Mobile package' summary card now reads 'Not ready' in warn tone; in 'Current authoritative dataset' click 'Generate mobile package' / 'Regenerate package' (138, 175) and wait for 'Mobile package generated for authoritative version X.' (86).

frictionPoints.problem: Five stacked sections (hero, summary cards, current dataset, import, versions, lookup) with the import form — the natural first step — in the fourth position, below the fold on a 13-inch laptop.
frictionPoints.whyConfusing: The page is organised by state rather than by task (RoadInventoryWorkspacePage.tsx:123-204); a newcomer wanting to 'publish a new version' has to discover that the sequence is import → publish → regenerate package by reading three separate section intros (115, 151, 186).

frictionPoints.problem: 'Authoritative', 'superseded', 'manifest', 'extract date', 'segments' vs 'rows', 'Dataset #14' vs 'version tag' are used without definition.
frictionPoints.whyConfusing: 'Authoritative version' (137), 'Loading authoritative manifest…' (153), 'Superseded — Available for rollback' (140), and the version table mixes 'ID #14', 'Version 2026-08-17', 'Rows' (192-195). The admin knows 'published dataset' from the job; the UI never uses that plain phrase except in the empty state (151).

frictionPoints.problem: Version tag is optional with no explanation of what is generated when it is left blank or whether it must be unique.
frictionPoints.whyConfusing: Placeholder only (RoadInventoryImportPanel.tsx:139-140); the resulting tag appears later in the versions table and in all notices, so a poor or auto-generated tag is hard to recognise.

frictionPoints.problem: Job card shows a raw monospace stage code and the polling cadence is invisible; a failure shows error_message but no retry guidance.
frictionPoints.whyConfusing: currentJob.stage is rendered verbatim (152); a newcomer does not know whether 'processing' will take seconds or minutes and whether they can leave the page (polling stops on unmount, 64-69).

frictionPoints.problem: Success text 'Dataset #14 is pending publication.' does not link to or scroll to the Publish button; the admin must find the matching row by ID in a 9-column table two sections down.
frictionPoints.whyConfusing: The import panel and the versions table are separate components with no cross-link (RoadInventoryImportPanel.tsx:154; RoadInventoryWorkspacePage.tsx:189-199). 'Publish' is an outlined text-xs button on the far right of a horizontally scrolling table (196).

frictionPoints.step: Publish is not the finish line
frictionPoints.problem: After 'Publish version' the field devices still cannot sync until 'Generate mobile package' is pressed in a different section above; the only cue is a sentence in the dialog and a red-toned 'Not ready' card.
frictionPoints.whyConfusing: The dialog's advice (RoadInventoryVersionActionDialog.tsx:67) disappears on close, the success notice says only 'Published…' (104), and the package button is inside 'Current authoritative dataset' (175) rather than next to the new row. A first-day admin can reasonably believe the release is done.

frictionPoints.problem: 'Refresh state' (page) and 'Refresh history' (import panel) sit on the same page with different scopes.
frictionPoints.whyConfusing: RoadInventoryWorkspacePage.tsx:130-131 vs RoadInventoryImportPanel.tsx:117-118; a newcomer does not know which one updates the versions table after a job finishes (the panel calls onDatasetChanged automatically, 81, but that is invisible).

frictionPoints.problem: 'Rollback' buttons (red) appear on every superseded row alongside 'Publish' on pending rows in the same Actions column.
frictionPoints.whyConfusing: Both go through the same confirmation dialog, which mitigates risk (RoadInventoryVersionActionDialog.tsx:59-63, 71), but a scanning admin may click the wrong row's action.

firstDayConfusions: Identity in the header is 'REVIEWER · ADMIN' — raw enum codes — so the user's first impression of 'who am I in this system' is an internal string (AppShell.tsx:157).

My Work for an admin is every step in the state, not 'my' work: triage panels, delegations, engineer drafts and all SUBMITTED assessments appear together and the first item auto-selected is a coordinator triage (MyWorkPage.tsx:52-61, 71, 88).

'Waiting on Reviewer' never resolves to 'you', and the admin flag grants Approve regardless of assignment, so the reviewer cannot tell which submissions were actually assigned to them (assessmentModel.ts:85-86, 131).

Two approvals with different names and outcomes: 'Approve submission' / 'Return for correction' → SUBMITTED/APPROVED/REJECTED on the submission, and 'Approve assessment' / 'Request revision' → SUBMITTED/APPROVED/REVISION_REQUESTED on the assessment; nothing links them (SubmissionDetailHeader.tsx:135-140; AssessmentDetailPanel.tsx:323-324).

Reviewer Note lives at the bottom of the submission page while the decision buttons that record it are in the top header (SubmissionReviewerSupport.tsx:24-35; SubmissionDetailHeader.tsx:133-142; SubmissionDetailPage.tsx:375).
The read-only technical form is a disabled editing canvas with drag/resize/full-screen tools, so review mode looks like a broken edit mode (SubmissionDetailPage.tsx:108, 762-794).

Same object, four names: Assessment, Submission, GISA form, GISA Sheet / technical submission; the nav says Assessments while the URL says /submissions and the page title is a location-date descriptor (AppShell.tsx:87; AssessmentDetailPanel.tsx:336; SubmissionDetailPage.tsx:765, 1169).

Role chips on the Users page are title-cased enum codes; legacy and canonical names may both be offered, and 'Field Worker' means engineer, not maintenance reporter (AdminUsersOperationsPage.tsx:8-10, 238-251; backend/app/roles.py:5-16).

On Road Inventory, 'Publish' is only the middle step; the mobile package must be regenerated separately from a section above, and the import success message does not lead to the Publish button (RoadInventoryImportPanel.tsx:154; RoadInventoryWorkspacePage.tsx:175, 196; RoadInventoryVersionActionDialog.tsx:67).

Irreversible decisions (Approve assessment, Request revision, Approve submission, Return for correction) fire on one click with no confirmation, whereas Publish/Rollback on Road Inventory do get a confirmation dialog — inconsistent risk signalling (AssessmentDetailPanel.tsx:323-324; SubmissionDetailPage.tsx:375; RoadInventoryVersionActionDialog.tsx).
mentalModelGaps: Job model: 'review' is a single decision on one assessment. Software model: there is an assessment state machine (SUBMITTED → APPROVED / REVISION_REQUESTED, assessments.py:1388-1443) and a separate submission state machine (SUBMITTED → APPROVED / REJECTED, SubmissionDetailPage.tsx:375), each with its own approve/return controls, and the UI never explains which is authoritative or whether one cascades.

Job model: a reviewer is someone assigned to a specific assessment (assessment_assignments REVIEWER/APPROVER). Software model on the submission page: review authority is the legacy global REVIEWER or ADMIN role (SubmissionDetailPage.tsx:161-163), so the submission page lets this user approve submissions they were never assigned to, while the assessment panel checks assignment except for admins (assessmentModel.ts:122-131).

Job model: 'my inbox' contains only what I must act on. Software model: My Work composes queues per role flag and the ADMIN flag lights every flag (roleModel.ts:32-73; MyWorkPage.tsx:52-61), so an admin-reviewer's inbox is the whole program's backlog with no 'assigned to me' distinction.

Job model: photos, map and form are one 'submission package' to read top to bottom. Software model: the map hero, a card canvas of disabled inputs, a 'Notes and actions' section, a 'Submission library', a separate photo-evidence route and a bottom card grid with Summary / Reviewer Note / Workflow History (SubmissionDetailPage.tsx:1211-1320) — the reading order interleaves authoring tools with evidence.

Job model: a role is a job title (Branch Chief). Software model: roles are enum codes with canonical/legacy aliases (GEOTECH_BRANCH_CHIEF vs BRANCH_CHIEF, GEOTECH_ENGINEER vs FIELD_WORKER) and the admin UI exposes whatever codes exist in the roles table, title-cased (AdminUsersOperationsPage.tsx:8-10; roles.py:49-56).

Job model: 'publish the road inventory' means field crews get the new data. Software model: publish changes the server-side authoritative version; field devices need a separately generated mobile package with a SHA-256, and the two steps live in different sections with no chained call-to-action (RoadInventoryWorkspacePage.tsx:79-93, 102-104, 175).

Job model: status words are plain English. Software model: submission statuses are raw enums ('SUBMITTED', 'REJECTED') and workflow history shows 'Event SUBMITTED · Actor user #12' (SubmissionDetailPrimitives.tsx:14-15; SubmissionReviewerSupport.tsx:52), while assessment states and events are humanised (assessmentModel.ts:51-68).
topFixes: Unify the review decision: one 'Approve' / 'Return for revision' pair that drives both the assessment and its submission (or hide the submission-level buttons when the submission belongs to an assessment), with identical labels, a required note field beside the buttons, and a confirmation step — remove the 'Revision requested.' auto-fill (AssessmentDetailPanel.tsx:294, 323-324; SubmissionDetailHeader.tsx:133-142; SubmissionDetailPage.tsx:375).

Give My Work an 'Assigned to me' default with kind/state filter chips (Triage, Needs delegation, Needs engineer, Drafts, Submitted for review, Ready to finalize) and change 'Waiting on Reviewer' to 'Waiting on you' when the signed-in user holds the assignment; for admins default to their assigned items and offer 'Show everything' (MyWorkPage.tsx:52-61, 139-170; assessmentModel.ts:73-92).

Add a true review mode to /submissions/:id: a read-only rendering of the GISA sheet (no disabled inputs, no drag/resize/full-screen toolbar), a sticky decision bar containing the Reviewer Note textarea and the Approve / Return buttons, and the photos + map placed before the form (SubmissionDetailPage.tsx:108, 762-794, 1211-1320; SubmissionReviewerSupport.tsx:24-35).

Adopt one vocabulary and humanise codes everywhere: title the page 'Submission #N · <descriptor>', drop 'GISA Sheet/GISA form' in favour of 'Technical submission', replace raw status enums and 'Actor user #N' with labels and names, and render header roles via a shared roleLabel() (SubmissionDetailPage.tsx:765, 1169; SubmissionDetailPrimitives.tsx:14-15; SubmissionReviewerSupport.tsx:52; AppShell.tsx:157).

On the Users page, present roles as a curated list with a one-line description each (e.g. 'GeoTech Branch Chief — assigns engineers to assessments'), show canonical names only and map legacy aliases behind the scenes, and add a password generator / show-hide toggle plus inline field errors (AdminUsersOperationsPage.tsx:8-10, 190-200, 209, 238-251).

Make Road Inventory a guided release: after a successful import show a 'Publish dataset #14' button in the job card, after publishing show 'Generate mobile package now' in the success notice, and surface the three-step sequence (Import → Publish → Generate package) as a stepper at the top; replace 'authoritative/superseded/manifest' with 'published/previous/current dataset' and humanise the job stage code (RoadInventoryImportPanel.tsx:152-154; RoadInventoryWorkspacePage.tsx:104, 123-141, 175, 196; RoadInventoryVersionActionDialog.tsx:67).

Fix the back path from a submission to its work item: '← Assessment #N' should return to /my-work?assessment=N when the user came from My Work, or the record view should carry the actions when the step is actionable, instead of the two-hop 'This step is yours — act on it in My Work' (SubmissionDetailHeader.tsx:78-79; AssessmentDetailPanel.tsx:267-270).
